chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, or someone else, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

There was a man in Makkah, a client of the Banu Umayya, called Ibn Abi 'Awanah, who had obstinacy (towards the Ahl al-Bayt). And whenever Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or one of the elders of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) entered Makkah, he would abuse him.
And indeed, he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was in the Tawaf, and he said, 'O Abu Abdillah! What do you say regarding touching the Stone?'
He (peace be upon him) said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touched it.' He said to him, 'I do not see you touching it.'
He (peace be upon him) said, 'I dislike that I should hurt the weak ones or be hurt (due to congestion).'
He said, 'So you have claimed that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touched it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'
'But it was so that whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was seen, they recognized his right for him, and as for me, they do not recognize my right for me.'

key_terms.أَشْيَاخُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Elders of the Family of Muhammad
key_terms.اسْتِلَامُ الْحَجَر: Touching the Stone (specifically the Black Stone)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) not touch the Black Stone directly during Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *Taqiyya* (prudent dissimulation) through Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) strategic avoidance of the Black Stone, not due to lack of reverence, but to prevent physical harm from the crowd who did not recognize his status. It highlights the distinction between the Prophet’s inherent authority, which commanded immediate respect, and the Imam’s need to navigate social dynamics while maintaining ritual correctness. This incident serves as a key scholarly reference for understanding how the Imams balanced public ritual observance with private spiritual intent and physical safety.
